name: Locations in Fisherman’s Wharf
description: 1- The Parliament.The Republic’s heart is its political core, symbolized by a grand white marble edifice representing peace and hope. It hosts public debates, but some chambers are exclusive for confidential parliamentarian discussions. Recently, bills regulating certain aspects of magic use and altering taxes on specific goods have heightened Parliament tensions, leading some to secretly hire mercenaries to intimidate rivals. 2- The Arena of Future. While no longer part of the judicial system, it remains a popular spectacle. Adventurers display their prowess in safe, magical, non-lethal bouts, seeking renown. Monthly tournaments in the Arena promise rich rewards, and victories here can elevate one’s status in the Adventurer’s Guild, unlocking more lucrative quests. Yet beneath its surface lies an inactive Vandanamalika, coveted by the Kemets and other powers. To activate it, specific pylons must be erected in the Storm Islands, Stravian, and Tsvetan. 3- Republic Military Fortress. Built atop a natural plateau, this fortress houses both magical cannons in its towering spires and the headquarters for the Freelands’ military forces. Sedura, the present Minister of Defense, devises strategies here that influence the entire army. Due to its key importance in defending the city from naval attacks, security here is reinforced. Nevertheless, the Kemets plot to disable the cannons, aiming to unleash their vast naval fleet to bombard defensive structures. 4- Prime Minister’s Palace. The palace is the home for the head of government and hosts meetings with diplomats and private talks with parliament members. It also serves as the administrative heart of many ministries and offices for the Republic’s state bodies. The Prime Minister traditionally holds a monthly gala here, attended by parliamentarians, wealthy merchants, diplomats, select nobles, and the families of those guests. These events are central to the Republic’s political maneuvers but are also exploited by groups like the Third Eye for negotiation, information gathering, intimidation, or even poisoning targets. 5- Celestianist Cathedral of Sun and Moon. High Cardinal Taram oversees the Republic’s primary Celestianist temple, having shifted the Church’s administrative heart from the sacred Skybell to Fisherman’s Wharf. Though Skybell’s cathedral remains grand and the city is considered sacred, Taram’s choice represents a shift from using Church’s wealth as a display of power to now aid the populace. This temple is now the epicenter for Church deliberations, where Cardinals gather for them. With the ever-present danger of Ungods’ servants infiltrating society and the Church, Taram and the cardinals remain watchful. He discreetly enlists hero groups proven loyal to Tamera and Bauron to investigate dubious figures in the city. 6- Fisherman’s Wharf Port.The Republic’s largest and most militarized port is vital for its citizens, providing an abundance of fish and seafood like squid, octopus, and oysters. Most trade ships engage with Kolbjörn, as the Republic’s main trade flows through the Central Seas’ Goldraft port. Fishing boat captains frequently post tasks in the Adventurer’s Guild, needing aid against threats like Kemet vessels, Sahuagin clans, the occasional kraken, or pirates responsible for vanishing ships. 7- Seabreeze District. This middle-class enclave houses merchants, artisans, fishing ship owners, military officers, and bureaucrats. It’s a serene district where children play in the streets and neighbors know each other by name. Businesses are restricted to those meeting basic daily needs, such as bakeries and small food vendors. 8- The Six Quarters.Surrounding the Parliament, this district boasts the city’s priciest estates. These grand homes belong to parliamentarians, nobles, and affluent merchants. No commercial endeavors are allowed. The sole non-residential structure is the esteemed Relic Hunters Guild headquarters, housing Tanares’ most renowned open museum. Given the guild’s collection of ancient treasures and vast knowledge from Tanares’ ruins, it is heavily defended, with many magical traps and mystical sentinels protecting its vaults. While heists have been attempted, the guild has consistently secured its relics. 9- Wallside District. Inhabited by winter elves, this district is eyed with mistrust by the city’s denizens, doubting the residents’ true loyalties. Though most are innocent winter elves, some Kemet spies blend in, masquerading as regular townsfolk. A concealed temple to Bás lies in a house basement where these Kemets convene to venerate their god. They covertly plan to bring frost to the farms, leading to food scarcity and city weakening. With discretion, they place secret shrines of Bás across the farmlands, awaiting the impending winter to activate their sabotage plan. 10- Uptown. Nestled among hilly terrain with uneven and sometimes steep streets, the area boasts diverse shops, homes, and artistically designed estates. The city’s open market thrives in the southeast on cobblestone grounds. Overlooking the market, atop a hill, stands the Adventurer’s Guild headquarters, a central hub for adventurers. Its mission board is perpetually filled, offering quests ranging from monster hunts to herb collections, merchant escorts through perilous areas, and even journeys to distant lands. Each task offers rewards proportional to its risks and duration, with values set by the quest givers. However, underpriced quests may remain unclaimed 11- Hope Square.Home to laborers and farming families, the district boasts modest dwellings, many crafted from resilient timber salvaged from the buildings destroyed during the Kemet Invasion. Those who lost their homes in the war resettled in Fisherman’s Wharf, naming this district. On its edge stands the Fisherman’s Wharf Academy of Magic, a symbol against the Empire’s stranglehold on the study of magic. While this district embodies hope, it also harbors a darker aspect. As this is one of the city’s most impoverished areas, crime is rife. Nights are treacherous, with muggings rampant and the murder toll exceeding the city’s combined. The government’s bid to strengthen patrols falters against the needed manpower and costs. Skirmishes between guards and criminals intensify, as these rogues band together, their menace growing. 12- The Cerulean Plaza. The commercial heart of Fisherman’s Wharf, this bustling market is brimming with local and imported wares. Adorned with inns, taverns, and the grand “Cerulean Cross Hotel,” the plaza boasts a uniform white and blue facade, enforced on the owners by fines. Celebrated as one of Tanares’ most beautiful marketplaces, its elegant shops, filled with exotic goods, attract many wealthy patrons, as well as bandits. With crime on the rise, shopkeepers, weary of the overburdened authorities, now turn to adventurers, offering rewards for reclaiming stolen items.
